Here $t\ne0$. Multiplying $x=t+\dfrac1t$ by $t$ gives

$$t^2-xt+1=0.$$

For a real parameter,

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=x^2-4\\x^2-4&\ge0\\x^2&\ge4.\end{align*}$$

Thus $x\le-2$ or $x\ge2$. Every such $x$ gives real, nonzero roots because their product is $1$. The range is $(-\infty,-2]\cup[2,\infty)$.
